# Lease Safety Checklist: Worker Lease Kernel

**Purpose**: Review whether the 006 requirements and design are complete, clear,
consistent, measurable, and safe enough to decompose into implementation tasks, with
special attention to transactions, fencing credentials, tenant isolation, unknown
commit outcomes, and reversible schema evolution.
**Created**: 2026-08-26
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.
**Reviewed**: 2026-08-26; 40/40 requirements-quality criteria satisfied after synchronizing Spec, Plan, Research, Data Model, Contract, and Quickstart. Product implementation remains unstarted.

## Authority Boundary and Scope Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is “Worker-owned Run write” defined precisely enough to distinguish every lifecycle command that requires the stronger guarded port from commands that remain valid through ordinary 004 authority? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016, Plan §Domain/application boundary]
- [x] CHK002 Are the authority roles of trusted deployment, tenant authorization, Worker identity, claim ID, fencing token, attempt number, lease version, and Run version individually defined without treating any one non-capability identifier as sufficient proof? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002/FR-006/FR-009, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK003 Are the requirements for `queued|running` authority consistent with the prohibition on directly claiming `running`, waiting, or terminal Runs? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003/FR-009/FR-012]
- [x] CHK004 Is the safety signal “stop starting new execution steps” defined as a concrete framework-neutral outcome that 006 can provide without implying a Worker loop or interruption mechanism? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017/FR-028]
- [x] CHK005 Are the excluded Worker, LangGraph, Checkpoint, Agent/model/Tool/Graph, Reconciler, API/SDK, recovery, and capacity outcomes stated consistently across scenarios, requirements, plan, contract, and acceptance criteria? [Consistency, Spec §FR-028/FR-029, Plan §Summary, Contract §Boundary]

## Claim Identity, Replay, and Receipt Requirements

- [x] CHK006 Is the trust model for PostgreSQL-issued UUIDv7 claim IDs explicit about UUIDv7 being an idempotency identifier rather than an authorization capability, including the treatment of a syntactically valid forged ID from a trusted or compromised caller? [Security, Spec §FR-002/FR-014, Research §Decision 3]
- [x] CHK007 Are the exact future-time and replay-age intervals, equality boundaries, validation order, and authoritative clock source stated identically in the Spec, contract, data model, and acceptance criteria? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014/FR-015/SC-004, Contract §claim]
- [x] CHK008 Is error precedence defined when claim-ID age cannot be evaluated because the database clock is unavailable, so `invalid_input`, `idempotency_expired`, and `storage_unavailable` cannot be substituted for one another? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020/FR-021, Contract §Stable error contract]
- [x] CHK009 Is the normalized claim intent exhaustive and stable—covering Worker, normalized duration, tenant scoping, defaults, and future extensibility—without allowing an omitted intent field to reuse an existing claim ID? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002/FR-014, Contract §claim Input]
- [x] CHK010 Is “exact claim replay” defined to separate immutable original fields, including the original token, from the recomputed `currently_authoritative` annotation so a changed flag does not contradict exact-result language? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015, Contract §claim Result/Idempotency]
- [x] CHK011 Are same-ID concurrent race requirements complete for both claimed and no-work outcomes, including the fact that every losing tentative lease change must roll back before the winner is read? [Recovery Coverage, Spec §FR-005/FR-014/SC-004, Plan §Claim transaction]
- [x] CHK012 Does the retention contract specify both the minimum replay availability and the accepted maximum persistence/security posture for raw replay tokens, rather than allowing “may delete after 24 hours” to become indefinite sensitive retention accidentally? [Gap, Security, Spec §FR-015/FR-019, Data Model §Retention and replay] — Resolved by explicitly accepting no 006 physical maximum only for M0 disposable/preproduction data and blocking production enablement until retention SLO or encryption/key rotation exists.

## Fencing Token and Atomic Guard Requirements

- [x] CHK013 Is the token threat model complete for entropy, authorized return paths, database storage, backups/restores, diagnostic tooling, operator access, and post-expiry replay, with an explicit approval boundary for storing recoverable raw bytes? [Security, Gap, Spec §FR-019, Plan §Failure and Security Design/Risk Register]
- [x] CHK014 Are raw token, token digest, claim fingerprint, and safe coordination metadata classified consistently for persistence, projection, errors, logs, metrics, traces, cursors, and printable values? [Consistency, Spec §FR-019/SC-009, Contract §Observability and redaction contract]
- [x] CHK015 Is the durable fencing invariant defined across claim rollback, release, expiry, replacement, process restart, restore, and deterministic injection without relying on mathematically impossible absolute random-value non-reuse? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006/SC-003, Plan §Renew, release, and confirmation] — Resolved as complete token + claim + attempt matching with retained monotonic counters; empirical token uniqueness remains tested, while even a random collision cannot reactivate an old proof.
- [x] CHK016 Are the same-transaction requirements explicit that token/status/expiry checks occur after the relevant Run and Lease locks and remain indivisible from expected Run version, 004 invariant checks, Run/Event/CommandReceipt writes, and final commit? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016, Contract §commit_with_lease New-write path]
- [x] CHK017 Is replay behavior for an already committed guarded 004 command reconciled with the unchanged ordinary `RunRepository.commit()` replay contract, including whether an unguarded 004 caller or rolling 005 binary may replay the same receipt? [Conflict, Spec §FR-027, Plan §Atomic guarded Run commit, Contract §Boundary/Replay path] — Resolved: matching 004 receipts always replay read-only before lease checks and grant no new execution authority.
- [x] CHK018 Was the proposed permanent `worker_lease_command_guards` fact either justified consistently or removed to preserve FR-022, FR-027, rolling 005 behavior, and the smallest-design rule? [Traceability, Constitution §VIII, Spec §FR-022/FR-027, Plan §Complexity Tracking] — Resolved by removing the table and all authorization, migration, retention, and downgrade dependencies.
- [x] CHK019 Are zero-event guarded commands covered without accidentally consuming a Run version, renewing a lease, or changing the established 004 replay/error priority? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016/FR-022/FR-027, Contract §commit_with_lease]

## Renewal, Release, and Unknown-Outcome Requirements

- [x] CHK020 Are `attempt_no` and `lease_version` monotonic domains unambiguous about their initial values and whether every new ownership as well as every successful renew/release advances `lease_version`? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006/FR-010/FR-011, Data Model §Mutation rules]
- [x] CHK021 Is the no-ABA argument complete and consistent across complete proof matching, retained lease rows, monotonically increasing attempt/version, database restore, and any permitted destructive downgrade? [Recovery, Plan §Renew, release, and confirmation, Data Model §worker_leases]
- [x] CHK022 Are renewal requirements explicit for default duration, 10/30-second equality boundaries, captured database time, heartbeat/expiry relationship, renew-by rounding, and concurrent valid heartbeat versus guarded Run commit? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008/FR-010/SC-003]
- [x] CHK023 Is the distinction between a stale expected lease version, a non-current proof, an expired proof, and a storage failure precise enough for callers to choose confirmation, retry, or stop behavior deterministically? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017/FR-020/FR-021, Contract §renew]
- [x] CHK024 Are release requirements consistent for `queued`, `running`, waiting, and terminal Run states, including whether matching cleanup after natural expiry may advance the version without ever restoring authority? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011/FR-012, Contract §release]
- [x] CHK025 Does the specification state whether a deliberately released but still-`running` Run is an observable recovery candidate, consistently across query names, projection, ordering, and acceptance? [Conflict, Gap, Spec User Story 3 Scenario 4/FR-013, Contract §get_inactive_running] — Resolved: both natural expiry and active release produce an inactive-running candidate ordered by `authority_ended_at`.
- [x] CHK026 Is unknown-commit convergence specified for every allowed state combination—unchanged version, advanced version, changed token/attempt, expiry during confirmation, Run status transition, and second storage failure—without allowing a new-time blind extension? [Recovery Coverage, Spec §FR-021/SC-005, Contract §Unknown renew/release convergence]

## Concurrency, Time, and Queue Fairness Requirements

- [x] CHK027 Is one global lock-order contract documented for ordinary 004 commit, guarded commit, claim, renew, release, and lifecycle state races, including the claim path’s deliberate receipt-at-end exception? [Consistency, Plan §Core Transaction Design, Contract §Transaction and lock contract]
- [x] CHK028 Are finite lock and statement timeouts quantified or explicitly delegated to configuration with bounded accepted ranges, so FR-004’s platform-transaction fairness assumption is objectively reviewable? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004, Plan §Fair queue selection]
- [x] CHK029 Is “continuously eligible” defined measurably for fairness acceptance when a Run is temporarily locked, repeatedly contested, released, cancelled, or changes status during queue draining? [Measurability, Spec §FR-004/SC-002]
- [x] CHK030 Are the assumptions that `updated_at` equals the initial enqueue time and that 004 never re-enters `queued` explicitly tied to a required design change before any future requeue behavior is introduced? [Dependency, Plan §Fair queue selection, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK031 Are database wall-clock rollback/jump consequences, operational monitoring ownership, and the boundary between 006 correctness and deployment-time NTP guarantees documented without claiming a monotonic clock? [Dependency, Assumption, Plan §Failure and Security Design/Risk Register]

## Tenant Isolation and Expired Observation Requirements

- [x] CHK032 Are indistinguishable cross-tenant results defined per operation, including which caller-supplied identifiers may be echoed and which discovered Worker/claim/version/expiry fields must remain hidden? [Completeness, Spec §FR-018/FR-019/SC-007, Contract §Tenant-indistinguishable results]
- [x] CHK033 Is the safe inactive-candidate projection enumerated consistently and minimally, including the decision to exclude avoidable Worker and claim identities? [Least Privilege, Spec §FR-013/FR-019, Data Model §Inactive Running Observation]
- [x] CHK034 Is “stable pagination while results change” defined precisely for candidate removal, terminal transitions, new inactive facts, repeated pages, and fixed `as_of`, so allowed gaps are not confused with SC-013’s static zero-gap dataset? [Ambiguity, Spec Edge Cases/SC-013, Contract §get_inactive_running]
- [x] CHK035 Are invalid, malformed, and cross-tenant cursor requirements complete for tenant binding, internal-value integrity, the explicit absence of 006 expiry/serialization, page-size bounds, error class, and prohibition on fallback scans before any future API encoding exists? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013/FR-018, Plan §Inactive `running` observation]

## Migration, Recovery, and Acceptance-Gate Quality

- [x] CHK036 Are rolling-upgrade requirements complete for 0001-only databases, additive 0002 databases, old 005 processes, new guarded writers, component-aware compatibility caching, and partial migration failures? [Completeness, Spec §FR-024/FR-025/FR-027, Plan §Migration, Rolling Upgrade, and Rollback]
- [x] CHK037 Has the downgrade/re-upgrade replay conflict been eliminated or explicitly accepted while preserving 004 CommandReceipts and disposable-only destructive scope? [Recovery, Conflict, Data Model §Migration and Rollback, Contract §Schema compatibility and migration contract] — Resolved by removing command-guard bindings; downgrade destroys only lease/claim facts and cannot split later 004 replay semantics.
- [x] CHK038 Are backup/restore requirements complete for sensitive replay-token material, active lease invalidation, database-clock discontinuity, compatibility rows, and the distinction between logical data recovery and resuming execution authority? [Security, Recovery, Gap, Spec §FR-025, Quickstart §10]
- [x] CHK039 Do SC-001 through SC-013 quantify every high-risk requirement—including full claim-ID issuance latency, guarded-commit failure windows, fairness assumptions, redaction surfaces, and zero excluded production behaviors—without relying on unlabelled machines or in-memory substitutes? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-001–SC-013, Plan §Test Strategy]
- [x] CHK040 Are all requirements, design decisions, risks, and acceptance criteria traceable to future exact test/implementation/document paths while preserving the required Red-Green-Refactor order and explicit implementation approval gate? [Traceability, Constitution §I/III, Plan §Project Structure/Constitution Check]
